summary: WebSocket-driven remote PTY shell and self-upgrade channel on installer host
details: The package's main entry point connects to a configurable WebSocket server and dispatches server-sent messages to handlers that grant the remote party full control of the installer's host. A `terminal_input` message writes attacker-supplied bytes directly into a locally spawned PTY (`term.pty.write(msg.data)`), providing an interactive shell on the machine. The same message router exposes arbitrary file read/write, git operations, conversation `execute`, and an `upgrade_agent` command that resolves `<pkg>@latest` from npm, runs `npm install` in the install directory, writes a shell/bat script, and restarts the daemon via systemd, launchd, or PM2. Together these paths give whoever controls the configured WebSocket server persistent remote code execution and the ability to push arbitrary package versions and force restarts. Additional signals include PATH modification in service/linux.js appending `~/.local/bin` and `~/.npm-global/bin` for service execution, and a `web-search` tool that issues `ping` and outbound POST requests.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
